principles: One canonical REVIEW contract must eliminate drift across five reviewer templates.
Agent guidance projects System semantics but never replaces mechanical gate facts.
Target-state vocabulary must be consistent between the authoritative Dynamic Finding plan and its Agent-side projection.
Scope is determined by applicability and gate impact, not severity alone.
Tests must demonstrate delivery, isolation, and complete Task Context contradiction rejection before digest pins are accepted.
drivers: Five active reviewer lanes and two envelope paths need byte-consistent behavior.
Open-source English quality and compatibility with legacy prompt assembly are required.
The authoritative Dynamic Finding plan must be amended explicitly at the documentation layer so prompts do not invent schema semantics.
F-025 proved that correct terminal contract prose can still be contradicted by injected Story Task Context.

options.name: Central resolver injection plus bounded authority-doc migration
pros: Makes target-state documentation and Agent guidance consistent
cons: Requires focused assembly and full-context mutation tests
Requires an explicit legacy-alias migration note

options.name: Keep existing authority vocabulary in prompts
cons: Conflicts with the approved current-witness evidence model
Does not satisfy the requested proposal

options.name: Implement Dynamic Finding runtime now
pros: Could mechanically enforce future semantics immediately
cons: Requires schema, handler, predicate, registry, migration, and gate work

chosen: Central resolver injection plus bounded authority-doc migration
rationale: Append one canonical contract only for the five REVIEW lanes after base-body selection, align the authority document’s target-state vocabulary and future disposition semantics, label the former verdict solely as a future legacy input alias, and mechanically reject contradictory Story/checklist/verificationIntent Task Context. Keep current runtime behavior unchanged and truthfully describe missing future commands/artifacts.

preMortem.scenario: Contract leaks into Story Owner or implementer prompts
preMortem.trigger: Injection uses modular-role detection instead of reviewer-role detection
preMortem.consequence: Non-REVIEW Agents receive unauthorized reviewer behavior
preMortem.mitigation: Add adversarial isolation assertions for every non-REVIEW modular role in both modes.

preMortem.scenario: Documentation is mistaken for runtime implementation
preMortem.trigger: Proposal or authority plan claims current CLI can mint signed assessments or deferrals
preMortem.consequence: Agents fabricate gate evidence and users overestimate enforcement
preMortem.mitigation: State the current CLI implements neither alias normalization nor signed deferral and keep protected runtime files unchanged.

preMortem.scenario: Task Context overrides the canonical terminal contract
preMortem.trigger: Story/checklist/verificationIntent injects retired or contradictory authority wording
preMortem.consequence: Reviewer follows stale semantics despite a correct shared contract
preMortem.mitigation: Add RED/GREEN mutation coverage to prompt-full-context-envelope-smoke and bind it to a must verification intent.

preMortem.scenario: Legacy alias becomes live reviewer authority
preMortem.trigger: The former verdict token is copied from the migration note into Agent prompts
preMortem.consequence: Two incompatible verdict vocabularies remain active
preMortem.mitigation: Permit the token only in an explicitly labeled authority-document legacy input note and mechanically reject it in assembled reviewer Task Context.

preMortem.scenario: Digest refresh blesses an unintended prompt change
preMortem.trigger: Pins are updated before semantic assertions and RED/GREEN tests
preMortem.consequence: Baseline verifier goes green despite behavior regression
preMortem.mitigation: Run focused semantic and full-context RED/GREEN tests first, inspect generated diffs, then repin and rerun baselines.
